name: אֱלִיאָב
summary: Borne by the leader of Zebulun in the wilderness, Eliab son of Helon, who brought Zebulun’s offering on the third day and led its host when Israel set out from Sinai (Num 1:9; 7:24; 10:16); by the Reubenite Eliab son of Pallu, father of Dathan and Abiram (Num 16:1; 26:8–9); by Jesse’s firstborn, whom Samuel thought to be Yahweh’s anointed (1Sa 16:6); by a Levite ancestor of Samuel (1Ch 6:12, called Elihu and Eliel elsewhere); by a Gadite warrior with David (1Ch 12:10); and by a Levite musician (1Ch 15:18; 16:5). It is אֵל “God” with the ־ִי of “my”, and אָב “father”: the two words David’s son is to say together, “You are my father, my God” (Psa 89:27).

evidence.note: Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Zebulun, אֱלִיאָב בֶּן־חֵלוֹן.
For Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon, among the men who stood with Moses and Aaron to number Israel.
Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, the Reubenite.
Samuel saw Eliab and said, “Surely Yahweh’s anointed is before him.”
Eliab, in the line of the Levites from which Samuel came.
Eliab among the Levites of the second rank, the musicians.
אָבִי אָתָּה אֵלִי: “You are my father, my God”, the name’s two words in one line.
“Have we not all one father (אָב)? Has not one God (אֵל) created us?”

note: BDB files the name under אֵל (a.dl.ai, among the words of the elah entry, root אלה); it is linked here to the av entry for its second element, אָב. The ־ִי may be the suffix “my” or a joining vowel (“God is father”); the names אֲבִיאֵל “my father is God” (1Sa 9:1) and אֱלִימֶלֶךְ show the same two patterns. TIPNR Elihu@1Sa.1.1 is the Levite of 1Ch 6:12 (Eliab there, Eliel 1Ch 6:19, Elihu 1Sa 1:1), so the bdb key limits the name entry to this spelling. TIPNR keys the Gadite as Eliab@1Ch.12.9 (English numbering; Hebrew 12:10).
